title: Game Math Part 2 · 3D Rotation 1: Orientation and Rotation Matrices

scenes.title: 이번 강의에서 배울 것
lines: Why can an object tilt while facing the same direction?
We will observe flight in a game and distinguish direction from orientation.
Then we will build a rotation matrix from three axes and convert local coordinates into world coordinates.
Finally, we will check inverse transforms and invalid rotations, then solve two problems to verify the signs and calculation order.

scenes.title: 비행을 볼 때 두 가지를 나누세요
lines: The character flies between structures in Superflight.
Watch the body's location separately from the direction it faces.
Its position changes, and its body also tilts as it passes obstacles.
Facing direction alone cannot tell us how far the arms are tilted.
One forward arrow carries less information than the body's full orientation.
Let us translate that difference into a simple set of axes.

scenes.title: 방향은 화살표, 자세는 몸 전체
lines: A direction vector is an arrow pointing somewhere. Twisting around its length does not change its direction.
Twist an object with wings around that same axis and the wings tilt. Its orientation has changed.
Two orientations can therefore share a forward direction but have different up directions.
A 3D unit direction can usually be parameterized by two angles, while orientation has three rotational degrees of freedom.
Orientation describes a state; angular displacement describes a change between orientations.
Both require a reference orientation and a coordinate frame.

scenes.title: 물체에 붙어 있는 세 좌표축
lines: Attach three small axes to the object. These form its local coordinate frame.
Red is x, green is y, and blue is z. These arrows follow the right-hand rule: x cross y equals z.
The three axes are mutually perpendicular unit vectors.
When the object rotates, its axes rotate with it, but their coordinates in its own frame remain unchanged.
To describe orientation, record where those local axes point in world coordinates.
Axis names and body-facing directions are conventions. Check your project's conventions first.

scenes.title: 몸의 위와 화면의 위
lines: Look at the flying character and the surrounding structures again.
It is easy to confuse the top of the screen with the character's local up direction.
When the body tilts, the screen's up direction still belongs to the camera's separate frame.
Compare structural edges, the torso, and the arms to distinguish those references.
Our calculation describes the relationship between the object's axes and the world frame.
The recording alone does not establish the game's internal rotation implementation.

scenes.title: 열벡터와 변환 방향을 먼저 고정
lines: We place vectors vertically and multiply by the matrix on the left: the column-vector convention.
Our matrix R converts a local vector into a world vector.
Its first, second, and third columns contain the local x, y, and z axes measured in world coordinates.
The book uses a left-handed frame and row vectors, so we must also check its axes and rotation signs.
Matrices for the same transform under these two conventions are transposes of each other.
Before trying a transpose to fix a picture, write down the input and output frames.

scenes.title: 90도 회전을 숫자로 계산
lines: Rotate by positive ninety degrees around z, using the right-hand rule: thumb along positive z and fingers following the rotation.
Local x becomes world y, so the first column is zero, one, zero.
Local y becomes negative world x, so the second column is minus one, zero, zero.
Local z remains unchanged, so the third column is zero, zero, one.
Multiplying the local vector two, one, zero combines twice the x-axis column with once the y-axis column.
The world result is minus one, two, zero. Matrix multiplication is a weighted sum of the transformed axes.

scenes.title: 로컬의 앞과 월드의 방향
lines: Watch the character turn as it flies beside the structures.
The body's local forward direction rotates with the body.
A direction defined in the world frame remains a reference even when the object's orientation changes.
Moving along the object's forward direction differs from moving along a fixed world axis.
A local-to-world matrix connects those two kinds of commands.
For now, focus on the coordinate frame rather than speed or collision.

scenes.title: 역방향은 왜 전치로 계산할까?
lines: Now express a world vector in the object's frame. We must undo the transform we defined.
With orthonormal local axes, the dot product with each axis gives the corresponding local component.
Multiplication by the transpose performs those three dot products at once.
Multiply world vector minus one, two, zero on the left by the transpose of the rotation matrix to recover local vector two, one, zero.
For a pure rotation the transpose is the inverse. This shortcut does not apply unchanged to arbitrary scaled or sheared matrices.
Points also include translation. To transform a point back, first subtract the object's world-space origin.

scenes.title: 방향코사인 행렬은 내적의 표
lines: A rotation matrix is also called a direction-cosine matrix. This is not a new kind of matrix.
It is a table of dot products between axes from two frames, all expressed in one common frame.
For unit vectors, the dot product is the cosine of their angle: one for parallel, zero for perpendicular, and minus one for opposite.
Under our column-vector convention, row and column indices correspond to world components and local axes.
Reading the first column therefore gives the three world components of local x.
Do not dot coordinate numbers measured in different frames. Express both axes in a common frame first.

scenes.title: 같은 물체도 다른 기준에서 보입니다
lines: The character moves while the camera shows its flight.
Observe the torso's tilt separately from the angle of background edges on the screen.
The object's world orientation is different from its orientation relative to the camera.
A different viewpoint changes the screen appearance of the same object.
To connect multiple frames, we need to know which frame each transform starts and ends in.
Let us connect those relationships through matrix multiplication.

scenes.title: 중첩된 자세를 하나로 합치기
lines: Let B transform a child object's local coordinates into its parent's frame.
Let A transform the parent's frame into world coordinates.
Applying B first and then A to a column vector is equivalent to the product A B.
The rightmost transform acts first. Labeling input and output frames makes the order easier to check.
A part attached to an aircraft goes from the part frame to the aircraft frame, then into the world.
Changing rotation order does not generally preserve the result. Next time we will compare two ninety-degree rotations directly.

scenes.title: 회전 행렬인지 확인하는 두 조건
lines: Nine numbers do not automatically make a rotation matrix.
First check that its three columns have unit length and are mutually perpendicular: the orthonormality condition.
In matrix form, R transpose times R must equal the identity.
A reflection also passes this condition. A proper 3D rotation must additionally have determinant positive one.
Check orthonormality and determinant positive one together.
With floating-point data, use a tolerance instead of exact equality. Choose that tolerance for the data and the intended use.

scenes.title: 회전과 늘어나 보이는 모습을 구분
lines: The character appears larger or smaller as its distance from the camera changes.
That visual change alone does not prove its rotation matrix contains scaling.
Perspective and camera distance also affect screen size.
Separate the body's 3D axes from its projected appearance.
The rotation matrix we are testing preserves lengths and angles of 3D vectors.
It does not require pixel lengths in screenshots to remain constant.

scenes.title: 반사와 스케일이 왜 통과하면 안 될까?
lines: Set the x diagonal component to two and the y and z components to one each. Only the x direction doubles, so length is not preserved.
Now change the x component to minus one and keep y and z at one. This produces a reflection across a plane.
A reflection preserves lengths and perpendicularity but reverses handedness.
Its determinant is minus one, so it must fail the proper-rotation test.
Flipping two axes is different: set x and y to minus one and z to one. This is a half-turn around z.
Do not judge from a single negative entry. Check orthonormality and the determinant together.

scenes.title: 작은 오차가 쌓이는 행렬 크리프
lines: Repeatedly multiplying small rotations each frame can accumulate floating-point rounding error.
Axes that were initially valid may drift slightly in length or perpendicularity. This is called matrix creep.
In code, measure orthonormality error and repair the axes when needed.
One method normalizes the first axis, removes its component from the second axis, then normalizes the second.
Constructing the third axis with their cross product preserves right-handedness. Degenerate input, such as nearly parallel axes, needs separate handling.
This correction handles small numerical drift. It does not automatically fix intentional scale or incorrect data semantics.

scenes.title: 부드러운 비행에도 계산 상태는 따로
lines: The character continues to move smoothly on screen.
Visual smoothness and mathematically valid internal data are separate questions.
During development, axis lengths and dot products can be inspected numerically.
We can monitor whether orientation updates increase the error.
This is an example of what developers can check, not a claim that this game has an error.
Next, we will connect this to storage costs and a clear code interface.

scenes.title: 행렬은 명확하지만 아홉 숫자를 저장
lines: Matrices directly support coordinate transforms and composition, and their axes are easy to inspect.
However, a three-by-three matrix stores nine numbers for an orientation with three rotational degrees of freedom.
Counting only 32-bit floating-point components, a matrix takes 36 bytes and three Euler angles take 12.
A four-component quaternion takes 16 bytes but has a unit-length constraint. It does not represent four independent rotation axes.
These figures count components only. Structure alignment and metadata may add storage.
Editing, storing many poses, and transforming vectors have different requirements, so multiple representations are often used together.

scenes.title: 코드에는 변환 방향을 이름으로
lines: Give the functions distinct names: localToWorld and worldToLocal.
The forward direction multiplies by R; the reverse uses its transpose for a pure rotation.
The names make the required input and returned output frames clear.
Points need translation added or subtracted. Direction vectors do not receive that translation.
Mathematical vector convention is separate from memory layout. Row-major storage does not by itself imply row-vector multiplication.
Check the library's multiplication and data-transfer conventions, then verify a small example with basis vectors.

scenes.title: 게임에서 명령을 표현하는 기준
lines: Now think about left and right relative to the flying body.
Screen-left can differ from the body's local left.
Some games use camera-relative input while others use object-relative input.
This is why direction variables should identify the frame their values belong to.
The recording does not establish the precise input mapping. We are connecting visible orientation changes to coordinate-frame concepts.
Next, we will examine what happens when we blend matrix entries independently.

scenes.title: 행렬 원소를 섞으면 회전도 될까?
lines: Suppose the starting pose is the identity and the ending pose is a 180-degree rotation around z.
The ending matrix has diagonal minus one, minus one, one.
Averaging corresponding entries halfway gives diagonal zero, zero, one.
This middle matrix collapses the x and y directions to zero. It is not a rotation.
Linear interpolation of matrix entries does not automatically produce a valid rotation path.
We will return to this problem in the quaternion and rotation-interpolation lectures.

scenes.title: 직접 풀어 보는 두 문제
lines: First problem: what happens when the ninety-degree z-rotation matrix acts on local vector one, zero, zero?
Select the first column. The world result is zero, one, zero.
Second problem: a world point is four, five, zero, the object's origin is three, three, zero, and its orientation is the same ninety-degree rotation.
Subtract the origin first to get world displacement one, two, zero.
Then multiply by the transpose to obtain local coordinates two, minus one, zero.
Check the result by rotating it forward and adding the object's position, returning to four, five, zero.

scenes.title: 이제 비행에서 자세를 읽어 보세요
lines: It is the same game, but we now have more specific things to observe.
Distinguish the body's position, its forward direction, and the tilt of its arms.
Also consider the difference between the camera's screen frame and the object's frame.
A rotation matrix records orientation through three axes and transforms vectors between frames.
We have not measured exact coordinate values from the recording, but we now know what to represent.
Next time we will study Euler angles and the order of rotations.

scenes.title: 오늘의 기준 세 가지
lines: Remember three things: a single direction does not determine a complete orientation.
Expressing three local axes in the same world frame gives a rotation matrix.
Always check input and output frames, the vector-multiplication convention, and the validity conditions.
Next time we will study rotation order, gimbal lock, and axis-angle representation.
